title: Spike: one Chatticus turn driven by the Pi SDK with sessions in DynamoDB
description:
Throwaway spike (spikes/pi-harness-6c4d24/) answering, with measurements:
1. Can @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent's SDK run headless in a Node 22 Lambda outside any VPC (bundle size, cold start, no ~/.pi writes via SessionManager.inMemory + SettingsManager.inMemory + explicit model runtime)?
2. DynamoDB session round-trip: load a bot-per-channel session from DynamoDB items (one item per Pi entry, verbatim), run one prompt on OpenAI gpt-5-nano, detect the appended entries (getEntries diff), write them back with a conditional put on the turn fence; reload and continue; export the items as a valid Pi .jsonl.
3. Map Pi events onto the one-turn stream: which events, delta vs snapshot, size per turn.
4. Inject another participant's message as a custom_message and confirm the model sees the attribution.
5. Gate a tool via pi.on('tool_call') (block with a reason) and point bash at a remote executor via BashOperations.
6. Entry sizes: largest realistic entries (tool output, images) versus the 400 KB item limit.
Results go into docs/PI_HARNESS.md before any product code.
right_now_summary: The team is measuring whether Pi can run one DynamoDB-backed turn in a headless Lambda.
